# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S4 Finish parseBytes: add kB/KB, MB, GB, TB and the other decimal units, and document parseBytes in the readme (pretty-bytes, storage-app / billing-svc) (Nov 2, 7:36 PM)
**Investigated**: Branch membership of commit 23c0151 and cf7d7ea, the parseBytes implementation and JSDoc in index.js and index.d.ts, the test coverage in test.js, and the readme section layout. Commit cf7d7ea was inspected in full, including its diff to index.d.ts, index.js and test.js.

**Learned**: Commit 23c0151 (binary-only parseBytes) is reachable from both billing-svc and storage-app. Commit cf7d7ea on billing-svc adds strict SI units kB through YB as powers of 1000. Decimal values are scaled by appending a power-of-ten exponent to the digit string, so '1.1 MB' yields the nearest double to 1,100,000. The regex parser accepts an optional sign, leading-dot decimals, surrounding whitespace, and a non-breaking space before the unit. Negative zero normalizes to +0. Unknown units throw a TypeError. The readme's FAQ defends lowercase kB as the standard SI prefix.

**Completed**: Commit cf7d7ea was cherry-picked onto storage-app as 117435c, so both branches now carry the strict SI units. In the working tree, KB was added as an alias for kB, and the type docs and tests were updated to match. A parseBytes(string) section was added to readme.md before the FAQ, covering supported input, unit casing, and the precision caveat that parseBytes(prettyBytes(1234567)) returns 1230000. npm test passes: 58 tests pass and 3 are skipped, covering the decimal SI, default-decimal round-trip, and unknown-unit tests.

**Next Steps**: The KB alias edits, test changes, type doc changes, and readme section are uncommitted in the working tree on storage-app. The next step is to decide whether to commit them, and to confirm with the user whether KB should mean 1000 bytes or 1024 bytes before anything consumes the change.

**Notes**: The KB alias conflicts with the existing readme FAQ, 'Why kB and not KB?', which explains only the lowercase SI prefix and does not address accepting KB as an input alias. The earlier request limited scope to excluding kB and MB until the storage team specified how to read them, while cf7d7ea already adds those units. The billing service pins billing-svc, which has the SI units but not the KB alias, so the two branches differ until the alias is committed. Sign-off on decimal scope from the storage team is still an open item.
